title: Deterministic attention epoch boundary race leading to prefix cache fragmentation
creator: Marco Chen
description: Symptom: a subset of long-running generation requests (prefill + decode, >1024 tokens) on dedicated clusters intermittently produce shifted token outputs and increased per-token loss without hardware faults. Behavior correlates with workload bursts where kernel-selection toggles between 'fused-attn' and 'attention-shard' variants at scheduler epoch boundaries. Observed state: prefix cache contains fragmented entries (misaligned start offsets) and attention scale accumulators show different FP16 head accumulators between prefill and decode paths. Hypothesis: a race at epoch boundary between the scheduler compactor (which coalesces prefix entries) and a kernel-selection path that swaps attention kernel implementations per-epoch. The compactor is not epoch-aware and can run while in-flight kernels are switching, producing partial writes into the prefix index and leaving stale per-head scaling state pinned to wrong token offsets, which leads to reproducible numerical drift and token misalignment when decoding continues. This is a correctness regression introduced after the scheduler optimization that aggressively rebinds kernels to improve throughput.
repro_steps: Spin up a dedicated pool with 4x A100-equivalent GPUs and runtime-1.22 with optimized kernel routing enabled
Load a mixed workload: 40% long prefill (1k-2k tokens), 60% short interactive decode; set scheduler epoch_size to 64 and epoch_compaction_enabled=true
Issue 200 concurrent requests with random seeds and identical prompts, collect decoded outputs and per-token logits
Search for shifted alignment in outputs and compare per-token cross-entropy against a golden run where kernel routing is pinned to a single kernel
Reproduce locally in the deterministic harness by forcing epoch boundary during an in-flight kernel-swapping window (test harness attached)
Attach runtime traces and flamegraphs for attention kernels when divergence happens
investigation_notes: Reproduced deterministically in our stress harness by toggling scheduler. Key observations: (1) When compactor runs concurrently with a kernel swap, prefix index entries are left with start_offset XOR'd with a stale epoch tag; (2) Attention per-head scale registers are not zeroed when switching from fused-attn to attention-shard, leading to accumulation of residual FP16 values on subsequent decodes; (3) Disabling compaction or disabling kernel hot-swap both independently eliminate the failure mode. Experiments: added atomic fencing around compaction prevented partial index writes but had measurable latency impact; pinning requests to an epoch (epoch pin) prevented state mixing with near-zero perf penalty in our canary tests. We measured an average per-token loss delta of 0.27 when the bug occurs and token shift of 1-3 tokens in generated outputs. No GPU driver errors were present.
decisions: Short-term: land per-request epoch pinning and gate compactor work behind an epoch-safe check to eliminate races. Medium-term: redesign compactor to be idempotent and use versioned prefix indices with compare-and-swap semantics. We will avoid global atomic fences in hot paths. Rollout plan includes canary on dedicated pools, followed by a staged rollout with telemetry. Add regression test to CI that randomizes epoch boundaries under load.
next_steps: Finalize and land PR #2786 (epoch pinning) with unit tests
Add compactor gating to ensure compaction only runs at epoch safe-points (PR #2810)
Create CI stress job that runs the repro harness nightly at scale
Run 48-hour canary on dedicated cluster with telemetry for token-shift metric
Update runtime docs describing epoch semantics and kernel-swap invariants
